rounds.text: National Plastic Technologies Ltd is fundamentally disconnected from its share price, trading at a modest P/E of 15x compared to a sector benchmark of 25.21x [E1, E6]. Long-term growth has been exceptional, featuring a 5-year compounded sales growth of 31% and an extraordinary 5-year compounded profit growth of 47% [E15, E19]. This robust performance generates high-quality earnings, backed by an impressive cash conversion ratio of 2.56x and Rs 23 Cr in operating cash flow for March 2026 [E34, E35]. Furthermore, return metrics remain strong, highlighted by a ROCE of 15.56% and ROE of 15.29%, both comfortably outperforming their respective sector benchmarks [E9, E10]. Conceded: the quarterly operating margin declined by 2 percentage points year-over-year in March 2026 and the 1-year share price return stands at -11% [E25, E31]. Nevertheless, insiders are showing confidence with promoters increasing their holding to 66.34% by June 2026, while a reverse DCF indicates the current market price of ₹ 231 prices in a modest 4.7% earnings growth [E2, E41, E46].

The fundamental momentum of National Plastic Technologies Ltd is showing clear signs of deceleration, evidenced by trailing twelve-month profit growth slowing to just 3% [E21] and a reported 30% year-on-year drop in net profit flagged by the screen engine [E63]. Operating margins have turned inconsistent [E32, E33], compressing by 2 percentage points in the most recent quarter down to 6% compared to the same period a year ago [E31]. This earnings contraction coincides with deteriorating technical and market momentum, as the stock languishes below its 200-day moving average [E49, E65] with a weak relative-strength rating of 32 against the Nifty 500 [E50] and a 1-year price return of -16.2% [E51]. Furthermore, the equity carries severe historical downside risk, demonstrated by an annualized volatility of 63.3% [E53] and a severe worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -79.4% [E52]. Conceded: the company trades at a reasonable P/E of 15x [E1] below the sector benchmark of 25.21x [E6], features a moderate debt-to-equity ratio of 0.87x with borrowings decreasing to Rs 52 Cr [E38, E39], and boasts robust long-term historical sales growth [E14, E15, E16].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth slowed to 3% [E21], net profit dropped year-on-year [E63], and margins compressed in the latest quarter [E31]. However, this cyclical softness overlooks exceptional cash generation, as operating cash flow reached Rs 23 Cr in Mar 2026 with a powerful cash conversion of 2.56x, ensuring profits are fully backed by cash [E34, E35]. Furthermore, borrowings actively decreased from Rs 60 Cr to Rs 52 Cr, supporting a moderate debt-to-equity ratio of 0.87x [E38, E39]. While technical indicators point to the stock trading below its 200-day moving average [E49, E65] and exhibiting a weak relative strength of 32 [E50], the underlying fundamental valuation trades at an attractive P/E of 15x compared to the sector benchmark of 25.21x [E1, E6]. This creates a stark disconnect where robust multi-year compounding—including a 5-year sales growth of 31% and profit growth of 47%—vastly outpaces the depressed 1-year price return of -16.2% [E15, E19, E51, E55].

Conceded: operating cash flow reached Rs 23 Cr in Mar 2026 with a cash conversion of 2.56x [E34, E35], and borrowings decreased from Rs 60 Cr to Rs 52 Cr [E39]. However, the bull's focus on multi-year growth figures like a 5-year sales growth of 31% and profit growth of 47% [E15, E19] masks a severe near-term deceleration, evidenced by trailing twelve-month profit growth plunging to 3% [E21], a net profit drop of 30% year-on-year [E63], and decelerating earnings growth [E64]. The cited P/E ratio of 15x compared to the sector benchmark of 25.21x [E1, E6] ignores the reality of margin compression, as quarterly operating margin fell by 2 percentage points to 6% in Mar 2026 compared to the year-ago quarter [E31], with an inconsistent yearly and quarterly operating-margin trend [E32, E33]. Furthermore, dismissing the technical weakness by pointing to a depressed 1-year price return of -16.2% [E51] is contradicted by the stock trading below its 200-day moving average [E49, E65], carrying a weak relative-strength rating of 32 [E50], and suffering from high annualized volatility of 63.3% [E53]. The moderate debt-to-equity ratio of 0.87x [E38] still leaves the company leveraged while facing an inconsistent margin profile and negative absolute price momentum that has yielded a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -79.4% [E52].
